functions.name: delete-group
functions.description: Delete a workspace group, subject to Notion's safeguard against leaving pages with no one having full access.

groupId.description: Opaque Notion group ID to delete from the connected workspace.

deleted.description: Notion acknowledged deleting the group; no restoration capability is implied.

FunctionOutput_notion_scim_deletegroup.description: Acknowledgment of the workspace group deletion.

tags.instructions: Find the group ID with `list-groups` and inspect it with `get-group` before deletion if needed. This deletes the group and its membership associations, not the members' accounts or workspace memberships. Notion forbids deletion when it would leave a page with nobody having full access. Recovery or restoration of the deleted group is not documented; do not assume deletion can be undone. Use `remove-member-from-group` to remove just one association.

This removes only the group association and may remove group-derived page access. It does not remove the person from the workspace. tags.instructions: Get the member ID from `list-workspace-members`. This removes workspace access and logs the person out of all active sessions; it does not delete their Notion account. The owner who created the current SCIM bot token cannot be removed this way. Removing another owner revokes tokens they created and can break integrations; arrange replacement tokens first. Use `add-workspace-member` for later provisioning, not as a promise to restore prior permissions.

tags.instructions: Find the member ID with `list-workspace-members` or read it with `get-workspace-member`. Supply only changes; omitted attributes are preserved. Null clears an optional profile attribute, and empty arrays clear multi-value attributes. Profile edits require verified ownership of the member's email domain. Photos cannot be updated through SCIM. Setting active=false removes workspace access; use `remove-workspace-member` for explicit removal and session logout. Use `add-workspace-member` for provisioning or a guest-to-restricted-member transition.
